title: Buildspace: how Farza grew a tutorial site into a story-driven school with 100K+ students
summary: Farza explains how Buildspace evolved from web3 tutorials into Nights & Weekends and a physical school by following its most motivated users. He covers selling a story instead of a community, building for shy beginners, hiring by conversation, and running a team with trust and no task board.

principles.text: Build the next product from your most motivated users: ask what they want after they finish.
principles.quote: we found that a lot of them wanted to keep going after nights and weekends we had nothing to do for them but that was not only our most valuable audience that was our most motivated audience

principles.text: Sell a story people can step into, not a community or a course.
principles.quote: I don't think we have a community I just think we have a story that we've loudly talked about and tell other people about and let them be a part let them be a character in the in the story

principles.text: Build for the unconfident beginners the market ignores, and design it for yourself.
principles.quote: it's always making stuff for the people that are already confident that are already like the doers and my thing is like I want to make it for myself

principles.text: Regularly make the team justify every product, and kill it if nothing changes.
principles.quote: if nothing changes I'm killing it I'm gonna shoot nights and weekends so I've been with a team every season I'm like give me 10 reasons we don't kill nights and weekends

principles.text: Hire through real conversation, not skill-set pitches.
principles.quote: a lot of times I got an interview and they'll just be like trying to tell me about their skill set I was like dude chill out like we just met like I don't care about it

principles.text: Run the team on trust: people state what they are doing, with no task board or top-down list.
principles.quote: I never show up on a Monday and have a list for people we don't have like a task management board
